_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909296.text: New York come in deflated after a 115-107 loss to Cleveland ended their five-game hold over the Cavs, and Mike Brown called Jalen Brunson getting no free throws "pretty alarming". Karl-Anthony Towns is playing through a sore calf amid stalled extension talks and trade chatter. Indiana got their first home win against Washington, but Tyrese Haliburton is still out and Aaron Nesmith is questionable with a sore knee. Both teams are 0-1 in their NBA Cup group, so neither can afford another loss. The mood is close to neutral, with a slight edge to Indiana's home bounce.

401909297.text: Milwaukee are 1-11 after eight straight losses and are closing in on the franchise's worst-ever start. First-year coach Taylor Jenkins has admitted "what we're doing right now is not working", and Kyle Kuzma has publicly demanded more urgency. Orlando just won two straight on the road for their first winning streak, with Franz Wagner scoring 71 points over those two games. They are still looking for their first home win under Sean Sweeney, and Paolo Banchero is still out. The Magic carry the better mood into this NBA Cup game, but their home drought is a mild counterweight.

401909298.text: Cleveland won at Madison Square Garden behind James Harden's season-high 32, easing some of the pressure on Kenny Atkinson. But Evan Mobley is out with a toe injury, his first absence of the season. Miami open a five-game homestand after a 3-2 West trip. Giannis Antetokounmpo is probable with a sprained wrist; he says he is "not concerned at all" and wants to move past Doc Rivers' public criticism. Giannis's edge and Mobley's absence lean slightly toward Miami.

401909299.text: Chicago have lost eight straight, are winless at home, and blew a 22-point lead to San Antonio on Wednesday. No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson fractured his right hand and faces surgery and about four to six weeks out, and Norman Powell is questionable with back spasms. Atlanta had three days to reset after the Lakers ended their four-game win streak, and this NBA Cup game opens a road trip. The mental lean is toward Atlanta; a Bulls team that keeps blowing leads is fragile late in games.

401909300.text: New Orleans have lost by 51 to Golden State and by 34 at home to Brooklyn in their last two games. Afterwards Zion Williamson called it "unacceptable" and told teammates and coaches to "look in the mirror". Trey Murphy III is out with knee soreness. Memphis have lost five of six since a 6-0 start, most recently 123-118 in Denver, where Tuomas Iisalo was criticised for not calling a late timeout. The Pelicans could respond to Zion's challenge, but a team this demoralised still leans toward Memphis.

401909301.text: Utah are 1-11 and badly short-handed, with Lauri Markkanen (hand fractures) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (MCL) out for weeks. Houston will be without Marcus Smart, who starts a three-game suspension for punching Charles Bassey. Bassey called it "fake toughness", so the episode may linger in the locker room. Rookie Darryn Peterson's run of 20-point games gives Utah something to play for. The mood still leans heavily toward Houston.

401909302.text: Golden State's eight-game win streak ended in Houston. Worse, an MRI showed Stephen Curry, who was second in the league in scoring, has an oblique abdominal tear. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks. The unresolved Kristaps Porzingis standoff adds noise on the second leg of a five-game trip. San Antonio have won ten straight, including a comeback from 22 down in Chicago. Without Curry the mental lean is clearly toward the Spurs.

401909303.text: Sacramento's locker room is visibly frustrated at 1-10. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. said "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun". De'Andre Hunter called the frustration "very high", and Zach LaVine asked for unity "from the front office down". Doug Christie is in the last fully committed season of his contract, and Domantas Sabonis trade talk lingers. Portland just beat Oklahoma City even without Ja Morant. The Kings could respond with pride at home, but the turmoil leans this toward Portland.

401909304.text: The Clippers are 2-8 after a 23-point loss in Phoenix, where Tyronn Lue said they lacked "defensive toughness". Lue has also ruled out Brandon Ingram's debut for this game. Oklahoma City have lost two straight and are thin: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace are out and Ajay Mitchell is questionable. They did just bring back Nique Clifford in a trade. OKC's urge to bounce back is the stronger pull.

401909980.text: New Orleans play the second night of a back-to-back amid a spiral that led Zion Williamson to call their recent blowouts "unacceptable" and demand accountability. Trey Murphy III has been sidelined by knee soreness. Denver are coming off a 123-118 win in Memphis, with Jamal Murray scoring 30 and Nikola Jokic adding 27, 11 and 8. They also won the earlier meeting by 13. Unless the Pelicans channel Zion's challenge, the mood and freshness lean strongly toward Denver.

401909981.text: Dallas were embarrassed 133-94 in Minnesota, which snapped their three-game win streak; Cooper Flagg managed 12 points two nights after scoring 43. A blowout like that often brings a sharper response. Cleveland are on the second night of a back-to-back after visiting Miami and remain without Evan Mobley (toe). The mental picture is balanced, with a slight lean to a motivated Dallas against a tired, short-handed Cavs side.

401909982.text: Detroit arrive buzzing after Cade Cunningham's career-high 52 points with zero turnovers in a double-overtime win at Washington, a historic line, alongside Ausar Thompson's first triple-double. They also beat Miami 128-111 in October. The Heat are on a back-to-back. Giannis Antetokounmpo is playing through a sprained wrist and brushing off Doc Rivers' criticism, which gives Miami some edge. Confidence and freshness lean toward Detroit, though the double-overtime minutes could take a little out of their legs.

401909983.text: Brooklyn come in with a lift after routing New Orleans 145-111. Noah Clowney, frustrated after losing his starting role, responded with 16 points, and Jordi Fernandez wants him to stay out of foul trouble. Memphis are on a back-to-back and only 2-4 at home. Tuomas Iisalo is under scrutiny for late-game decisions, though Ty Jerome is on a run of 20-point games heading into free agency. The lean is mild toward Memphis, with the fatigue and home struggles keeping it close.

401909984.text: Minnesota have won five straight without Anthony Edwards, capped by a 133-94 rout of Dallas in which LaMelo Ball and Bones Hyland combined for 46 points. Chicago are on a back-to-back after hosting Atlanta. They have lost eight straight and just lost No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson to a fractured hand for about four to six weeks. The only mental caution for Minnesota is a look-ahead to Portland. The lean is heavily toward the Wolves.
